public_rationale: The Guardian’s report published March 11, 2025 describes a Grok user encountering missing pellets, broken warp tunnels and problematic ghost behavior [e1]. He reported frustrating debugging and switched to Tetris after an hour [e1]. The same user called the experience “surprisingly easy,” while another reported getting a rough version in seconds that still needed corrections [e2]. These accounts show both rapid initial results and functional problems, but do not settle the general claim about contemporary AI coding tools [e1] [e2].
limitations: Both evidence items come from one article about Grok, without a comparison across tools [e1] [e2].
The publication date is known, but exact trial dates and model versions are not established for March 1–14, 2025 [e1] [e2].
The accounts do not provide consistent functional checks, reproducible success rates or complete records of corrective work [e1] [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI coding tools find it hard to correctly build even a simple program like Pac-Man.

statement.excerpt: And I pointed out that even something as easy as Pac-Man was pretty hard to get right with current tools.
statement.document_title: Hype, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, the podcasters who love him — and how the New York Times’ commentary on AI has degenerated into industry cheerleading

from_speaker: even something as easy as Pac-Man
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading concerns material functional difficulty producing a basic playable Pac-Man-style game with contemporary AI coding tools.
It does not assert impossibility, require an exact arcade reproduction, or imply that every attempt fails.
Current tools is operationalized as tools available in the first half of March 2025, through the post date.
A general statement about tools requires more than an isolated failure or an isolated successful demonstration.
criteria.support_condition: Documented, adequately dated trials across relevant contemporary tools show substantial gameplay errors or considerable corrective intervention under ordinary prompting.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable trials show that those tools reliably produce functionally correct basic implementations with little corrective intervention.
